items.title: Nothing in CI compiles the GPU or webview crates for macOS, and the nightly macOS perf job is dead (N209): macOS is the one release target with no check at all before a user's machine
items.discussion: lane hw-58, 2026-11-17 (F187): `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` of `crates/vilan-rt-gfx` passes for `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-apple-darwin` from Linux once the rustup targets are added (nothing in the GPU stack compiles C); `crates/vilan-rt-webview` cannot be checked from Linux: `objc2-exception-helper` 0.1.1 (through wry and objc2's `exception` feature) compiles Objective-C with the target's C compiler
items.area: .github/workflows/ci.yml (job `gfx`), scripts/ci-local.sh (`leg_windows`, which already cross-lints the workspace, gfx and webview for msvc), crates/vilan-rt-webview
items.body: Two additions, both small: (1) cross-lint the GPU crate for `aarch64-apple-darwin` on the Linux runner beside the Windows cross-lint (it needs only `rustup target add`; seconds once cached); a local leg `macos` in ci-local.sh the way `windows` is one, with the same honesty: it proves the tree BUILDS for that target and nothing about what it does. (2) the webview crate needs a real `macos-latest` runner for even a `cargo check`; one job, check only, on pushes that touch `crates/vilan-rt-webview` or its lockfile. The release workflow builds the compiler for both Apple targets, so the compiler itself is covered; the runtime crates a user's native build links are not.

items.title: Two rough edges in every native build, seen preparing the hardware run: the emitted Rust has unreachable code after `process::exit` (warnings in every generated project), and the printed binary path lacks `.exe` on Windows
items.discussion: lane hw-58, 2026-11-17 (F187): `cargo check` of the generated `ui-counter` project for msvc and for aarch64-apple-darwin passes with two `unreachable_code` warnings from the emitter, not the target
items.area: crates/vilan-rust/src/lib.rs (what follows a diverging host call), crates/vilan-cli/src/native.rs (`cargo_build`'s returned path)
items.body: (1) After `vilan_rt::process::exit(2)` the emitter still writes the unit value (`vilan_rt::str_new("")` in the sample), so rustc warns `unreachable expression` on every build of a program that exits; the emitter knows the callee diverges (the analyzer types it `never`) and should end the block there. A generated project that builds without warnings is worth holding with a pin: `RUSTFLAGS=-D warnings` over the native differential's shared target would have caught this. (2) `cargo_build` returns `target/debug/<name>` on every system; on Windows the file is `<name>.exe`. Launching works (the process launcher appends the extension, and CI's Windows shards run native programs), but the path `vilan build --backend rust` PRINTS is not a file that exists. Use `std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX`. Related, not a defect but a decision for the desktop work (F166): no `windows_subsystem` attribute is emitted, so a GUI program is a console program on Windows: double-clicked, it opens a console window beside its own.
